problem: Existing VLN surveys focus on traditional (non-LLM) VLN settings and give limited coverage of LLM/VLM-based VLN, especially Sim2Real transfer and edge-oriented deployment.
motivation: LLMs and VLMs have substantially improved instruction interpretation, cross-modal alignment and reasoning-based planning in VLN, moving the field from geometry-driven to semantics-driven to knowledge-driven approaches. A structured review is needed that also covers practical deployment concerns (edge, Sim2Real) and the task evolution toward goal-oriented and demand-driven navigation.
key_idea: A structured survey of LLM-enabled VLN organized around four components (instruction understanding, environment perception, high-level planning, low-level control), plus edge deployment, datasets, evaluation protocols, challenges and future directions.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or experiments can be cited. The abstract's conclusion is that LLM-driven VLN is moving toward deeper cognitive integration, which supports more explainable, generalizable and deployable embodied navigation. It names reasoning complexity, spatial cognition, real-time efficiency, robustness and Sim2Real adaptation as the main open challenges.
method: Four-component taxonomy: organizes LLM-enabled VLN into instruction understanding, environment perception, high-level planning and low-level control.
Deployment analysis: summarizes edge deployment and implementation requirements, and Sim2Real considerations.
Datasets and evaluation: summarizes datasets and evaluation protocols.
Task evolution analysis: traces the shift from path-following to goal-oriented to demand-driven navigation.

Challenges and outlook: discusses reasoning complexity, spatial cognition, real-time efficiency, robustness and Sim2Real; proposes future directions of knowledge-enhanced navigation, multimodal integration and world-model-based frameworks.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey paper with no reported experimental results
results: This is a survey and reports no quantitative results. Its main claim is that LLM-driven VLN is progressing toward deeper cognitive integration, and it fills a gap left by earlier surveys on LLM-based VLN, Sim2Real and edge deployment.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the depth and coverage of the review cannot be verified.
As a survey, it provides no new method or empirical validation.
